A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GACD research, with matching authors, core experiments, and substantial supplementary material. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison across the reorganized sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original GACD evaluations on AMBER, MSCOCO, POPE, and other benchmarks, alongside component ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, comparator results, a token-grouping ablation, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The gradient-influence, noun-grouping, contrastive-decoding, and early-stopping pipeline remains recognizable. However, v3 Eq. 8 omits the noun-specific output index used in v1 Eq. 7, and v3 explicitly requires nonnegative decoding weights. The PDFs do not establish whether these are procedural changes or imprecise reformulations and clarifications.

E1.justification: v3 supplementary Section 7 adds ScienceQA and VizWiz evaluations, extending coverage to structured science reasoning and questions from blind users involving poor-quality images and unanswerable cases. Earlier benchmark coverage is retained. These additions broaden represented domains and input conditions, rather than merely changing model configurations.

E2.justification: v1 Table 6 compares only the unmodified model and GACD for LLaVA-v1.6 and InternVL2; v3 supplementary Table 1 adds RLAIF-V, VCD, M3ID, and AVISC to those comparisons. Supplementary Table 10 also introduces PAI and Middle as captioning comparators, while Table 17 adds a VCD computational comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds Qwen2-VL as an AMBER evaluation backbone and a separate LLaVA-v1.5 comparison using a 12% early-stopping threshold rather than the retained 7% default. It also introduces TFLOP measurement on POPE. Existing benchmark protocols, generation limits, and sampling settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a top-1 versus top-2 influential-token grouping ablation and extends the early-stopping trade-off analysis with the 12% comparison. Computational overhead receives a quantitative comparison. The gradient-method and norm ablations moved into the main text already existed in v1 Appendices K–L; other established analyses remain.

E5.justification: The non-greedy sampling results retain the same uncertainty values in v1 Table 12 and v3 supplementary Table 8. Figure 3 retains mean and standard-deviation reporting for visual influence. Neither version adds or changes disclosed run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, but v3 adds substantial result entries. New baseline/GACD comparisons report 66.2/68.7 on ScienceQA and 48.7/52.8 on VizWiz, plus Qwen2-VL and additional comparator scores. New results also cover top-2 grouping, 12% early stopping, and TFLOPs of 9.68/19.37/19.49 for baseline/VCD/GACD. These are additional conditions and measurements, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: v3 replaces v1's identification of the output sequence with a softmax expression by an explicit categorical next-token formulation and states nonnegative decoding-weight constraints. Supplementary Section 2 extends the KL expression from v1's text-only reference example to an object-conditioned reference. The underlying Taylor approximation remains, with no new theorem.

C1.justification: The contribution summary narrows 'without sacrificing information' to maintaining a 'favorable balance between accuracy and informativeness.' The central claims of jointly mitigating both biases without auxiliary models or fine-tuning remain, as do the introduction's headline benchmark improvements.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit discussion of how shortening responses can confound CHAIR comparisons and explains top-1 grouping through concentrated versus diffuse attributions. It replaces the up-to-five-times computational-cost interpretation with approximately doubled POPE TFLOPs, without reconciling gradient accounting. The white-box limitation is retained and moved into the main text.

D1.justification: v3 newly states that the visual encoder runs once and the second pass uses few tokens, and documents the additional 12% threshold and TFLOP measurements. Existing GPU, batch size, generation limits, spaCy noun detection, autograd implementation, and evaluation-repository information remain; their relocation does not constitute new disclosure.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of LPOI's object-aware approach and attention-based interventions, contrasting their layer selection and model-specific adjustments with GACD. References also expand for new benchmarks and comparators, while several peripheral citations disappear. The central positioning around inference-time, object-aware bias mitigation remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and method exposition are substantially rewritten. 'Contrastive' becomes 'Constrained' in GACD's name, and the method is organized into two named components. Experimental subsections and supplementary sections are reorganized, with gradient/norm analyses and limitations moved into the main text.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 is redrawn, Tables 2 and 5 are reorganized into stacked model blocks, and existing figures and tables are resized or relocated. The supplement expands the modern-model table and adds displays for new benchmarks, early stopping, token grouping, and computational cost.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons strengthen evidence for generalization beyond the earlier evaluations, and the top-2 ablation directly supports the grouping choice. The qualified accuracy–informativeness claim also improves calibration. Gains remain limited: the new early-stopping comparison lacks comparator recall and length, computational accounting is not reconciled with v1, and the rewritten masking notation introduces ambiguity.
